Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with `README.md`, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both wake-policy skill instructions. I’m using the fish-control skill because the transfer protocol explicitly requires it, and the visual-signals skill because this policy must be grounded in both current 3D wake views before any edit.

The workspace is a fresh lineage with one sampled parent: a finite but poor `left_domain` rollout. I’m now anchoring the images to its trajectory, flow/load metrics, diagnostics, inherited notes, and exact seed controller; only after that will I translate one bookshelf invariant into a candidate hypothesis.

The visual-signals skill changed the diagnosis: this is self-propelled, not advected, but its alternating 3D vortex trail accompanies an uncontrolled yaw excursion and upward exit after only `8.55T`; distance improves just `0.25L` at best and ends worse. The missing capability is target-relative yaw regulation, while the existing autonomous oscillator is worth preserving as the propulsion carrier. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a bounded steering mechanism, not scalar-only tuning.

The bookshelf primitive I’m carrying forward is mean-curvature steering modulated by closed-loop direction feedback. Here that becomes a bounded posterior-joint mean bend driven by body-frame bearing plus short-window bearing trend, layered on the unchanged state-feedback traveling-bend carrier. Exact published gains and gait details are not being transferred. I’m recording this hypothesis before touching the solver, as required.

The candidate now keeps the sampled propulsion dynamics unchanged and adds only the bounded posterior mean-curvature loop. I’m distilling the reusable lesson into guidance next: a coherent alternating wake and finite self-propulsion did not imply route control here, so later workers should distinguish carrier quality from bearing regulation before tuning drive.

Both required files are updated, so the candidate is materially complete. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated check runner now; it will compare guidance against the assigned parent, exercise the Julia policy contract, and enforce the editable-file boundary without running CFD.

The first invocation was rejected because the checker’s fixed role cannot inherit a full conversation fork. I’m relaunching it with the same bounded validation task and no context fork; the checker reads the workspace contract directly.

The mandated checker role is unavailable in this account because its fixed model is unsupported. The invocation itself failed before any check ran, so I’m applying the documented fallback directly: I’ll execute its three non-CFD checks separately and repair any failure before finishing.

The guidance check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned guidance parent twice, so the checker refuses to identify a unique parent before it even compares our lesson. I’m inspecting the checker’s matching rule, then I’ll make the smallest in-workspace repair needed to restore the single-parent marker.

All three prescribed checks now pass: guidance delta, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. I’m doing one final dry semantic probe of the steering law—checking sign symmetry, boundedness, and that every referenced parameter is declared—then I’ll hand off without running CFD.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded bearing-and-trend mean-curvature steering over the preserved oscillator.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:51): reusable lesson distinguishing coherent propulsion from target control.

All non-CFD checks pass: guidance delta, Julia contract, parameter schema, steering boundedness/symmetry, and solver boundary. I also removed a duplicated parent marker in [README.md](README.md:102) that initially prevented the mandated guidance check. No CFD was run.
